However, she now complains of daily symptoms and once per week symptoms at night time. A forced expiratory volume in 1 second test shows 70% of normal. Which of the following medication regimen is now most appropriate?
choices: Long acting beta2 agonist and inhaled glucocorticoids

question: A 28-year-old woman G 4 P2012 immigrant presented to the Maternal Health Clinic at 20 weeks' gestation with a cough and night chills for the past month. The cough is productive and produces thick sputum. She had been prescribed treatment by a general practitioner for the cough and it had not responded to treatment. Patient nail beds and conjunctiva appeared pale and the cervical lymph nodes are palpable. Auscultation of the chest shows crepitation over the upper left lobe. She had received a BC vaccine as a child. A blood test is positive for interferon-gamma release assays. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 84 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.5° C oral Which of the following is the next best step in obtaining a definitive diagnosis?
A 23-year-old primigravida presented in labour. The mid wife advised mediolateral episiotomy during the 2nd stage of labour. What is the advantage of a mediolateral episiotomy?

A 23-year-old G2 P1001 at 22 weeks' gestation presented with a complaint of her abdomen is larger than her previous pregnancy (see report). Ultrasound: Showed dizygotic twin pregnancy. Which of the following best described membranes and placenta of dizygotic twins?
choices: Monochorionic and monoamniotic for conjoined twins
Monochorionic and diamniotic for the foetuses of same sex
Dichorionic and monoamniotic for the foetuses of same sex
Dichorionic and diamniotic regardless of the sex of the foetuses

question: A 25-year-old woman has delivered a boy. On inspection of the umbilical cord, a single artery was noticed. Which of the following is associated with the above finding?

A 33-year-old pregnant woman G4 P2012 at 38 weeks' gestation presented with a complaint of dizziness, light-headedness and fainting sensation especially in bed for 2 weeks duration (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 100 /min, Respiratory rate 24/min, Temperature 36.6° C Test Result Normal Values Hb 95 120-160 g/L WBC 9 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Platelet count 200 150-400 × 109/L Which of the following is the best management?
A 28-year-old woman is diagnosed with an ectopic pregnancy. Which of the following is the most likely predisposing factor?
choices: Use of an intrauterine contraceptive device

question: A 21-year-old woman G2 P1001 presents to the Emergency Room with a severe lower abdominal pain for 1 day. Pain is dull and intermittent that last for 10-15 minutes and associated with nausea and vomiting. Examination confirms tenderness and guarding in the lower abdomen, it is more on right side and slight fullness in the right iliac fossa (see report). Blood pressure 90/60 mmHg Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 13 /min Temperature 37.6° C Pregnancy Test: Negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old pregnant woman at 34 weeks of gestation presented with labour pains. On physical examination, the cervix was 4 cm dilated. Cardiotocography was performed (see image). Blood pressure 135/88 mmH Heart rate 89 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.4" C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman G3 P0020 at 5 weeks' gestation presents with vaginal bleeding associated with some blood clots that has started 3 hours ago. She had been diagnosed with cervical incompetence in her 2 prior second-trimester abortions. A history of dilatation and curettage in her last abortion declared. On examination; the cervical os is open and no on-going bleeding. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her current diagnosis of vaginal bleeding?

A 59-year-old woman comes to the clinic with headache, dyspnea on exertion and occasional palpitations (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Hb 95 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) MCV 68 80-95 f1 Platelets count 530 150-400 x 109/L Total iron binding capacity 30 11.6-31.3 mol. (Male) 9-30.4 pmol/L (Female) Ferritin 3 20-300 g/L (Male) 20-120 pg/L (Female) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old woman comes to the clinic with headache, dyspnea on exertion and occasional palpitations (see lab reults). Test Result Normal Values Hb 95 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) MCV 68 80-95 fl Platelets count 530 150-400 x 109/L Total iron binding capacity 28 11.6-31.3 mol/. (Male) 9-30.4 umol/L (Female) Ferritin 3 20-300 pg/L (Male) 20-120 pg/L (Female) Apart from starting iron supplement, which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 46-year-old man comes to the clinic with dyspnea on exertion and palpitations. On examination, he has patches of vitiligo (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Hb 89 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) MCV 103 80-95 fl Platelets count 128 150-400 x 109/L Ferritin 105 20-300 g/L (Male) 20-120 g/L (Female) Vitamin B12 (Men) 122 160-900 ng/L Folic Acid (Men) 8 <4 ug/L Which of the following is the most appropriate test to be ordered next?

A 59-year-old man has unsteady gait. On examination, he has decreased proprioception in the lower limbs with positive planter reflexes (positive Babinski) and absent ankle and knee's reflexes. He has anemia. Peripheral smear done (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old-woman has decreased concentration (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Hb 89 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) MCV 106 80-95 f1 Platelets count 129 150-400 x 109/L Vitamin B12 (Women) 0,46 0. 12-0.66 mol/L Folic Acid (Women) 0.03 <0.1 umol/L Which of the following would be found on further testing?
choices: High methyl malonic acid and normal homocysteine
High methyl malonic acid and high homocysteine
Normal methyl malonic acid and high homocysteine
Low methyl malonic acid and low homocysteine

question: A 46-year-old man has dyspnea on exertion and palpitations. On examination, he has patches of vitiligo and has absent reflexes with positive Babinski in the lower limbs (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Hb 91 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) MCV 103 80-95 f1 Platelets count 129 150-400 × 109/L Ferritin 120 20-300 g/. (Male) 20-120 g/L (Female) Vitamin B12 (Men) 124 160-900 ng/L Folic Acid (Men) 6 <4 ug/L Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 35-year-old woman has fever and headache for 2 days. On examination, she has a scattered petichiae over her body. Her platelets are 32. Peripheral smear done (see image and lab results). Temperature 38.6 °C Test Result Normal Values Platelets count 32 150-400 x 109/L Hb 11.2 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) MCV 102 80-95 f1 Reticulocyte 4.9 0.2-1.2 % Lactate dehydrogenase 690 60-160 IU/L Indirect bilirubin 43 3.2-12.1 umal/L Total bilirubin 65 3.5-16.5 mol/L Creatinine 66 44-115 mol/L APTT 36 30-40 sec INR 1.1 0.8-1.2 Prothrombin time 11 10-13 sec Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old woman has fever and headache for 2 days. On examination, she has a scattered petichiae over her body. Peripheral smear done (see image and lab results). Temperature 38.6 °C Test Result Normal Values Hb 112 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Reticulocyte 5.6 0.2-1.2 % Platelets count 32 150-400 x 109/L Indirect bilirubin 48 3.2-12.1 mol/L Total bilirubin 76 3.5-16.5 mol/L Lactate dehydrogenase 690 60-160 IU/L APTT 33 30-40 sec INR 1.0 0.8-1.2 Prothrombin time 10 10-13 sec Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 48-year-old man develops right popliteal vein thrombosis post-sleeve surgery. He is started on enoxaparin and warfarin. What is the target therapeutic international normalization ratio range for this patient?

A 53-year-old woman admitted to the hospital with pneumonia. She has diabetes, hypertension and is on hemodialysis for end-stage renal disease (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Hb 98 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 151 150-400 x 109/L APTT 33 30-40 sec INR 0.9 0.8-1.2 Prothrombin time 9.8 10-13 sec Creatinine 460 44-115 mol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate venous thromboembolism prophylaxis for this patient?

A 38-year-old woman admitted with pyelonephritis. 2 days after admission, she develops sudden severe shortness of breath (see report). Blood pressure 84/50 mmHg Heart rate 124 /min Oxygen saturation 84 % CT-pulmonary angiogram: A saddle embolus at the bifurcation of the pulmonary artery and multiple segmental pulmonary emboli bilaterally. which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 59-year-old man has diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia and chronic renal impairment. He was admitted 5 days ago to the Coronary Care Unit for a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). He is receiving unfractionated heparin. His labs upon admission were normal. Day 5 of his admission, labs as shown (see lab results). Low fat diet to produce 5-10 % weight loss
Diet is less effective than metformin to reduce the risk of diabetes
Low carbohydrate diets are more likely than low fat diets to prevent diabetes in the long-term

question: A 40-year-old man comes to the clinic for evaluation and management of obesity. His obesity is complicated by type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), hypertension, sleep apnea, dyslipidemia, chronic low back pain, osteoarthritis of the knees, and depression. He was prescribed medications for these problems but that he is not compliant to treatments. His wife accompanied him to the visit was anxious about his health and she want the doctor to council him for the best solutions he can do. BMI 55 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most appropriate advice will help in treating this patient?
choices: Emphasizing the importance of adherence to his medications
Referral to an orthopedic surgeon for knee arthroplasties

question: A 39-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes for 20 years was married recently; she and her husband want to get pregnant. The woman has hypertension treated with an angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor and a diuretic with maintenance of blood pressure at 118/80 mmHg. Her insulin doses are all administered through a continuous insulin infusion pump using insulin aspart. She reported that she would try to become pregnant next month (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values 24 hr urine protein 2000 0.8-14 mg/di (Male) 2.5-11 mg/dI (Female) Creatinine 88 44-115 mol/L HbA1C 8.0 4.7-5.6 % What is the best advice at this moment to control her blood sugar and prevent congenital malformation?
choices: Eliminate snacks and begin to take 3 heavy meals daily
Substitute an angiotensin receptor blocker for her ACE inhibitor
Her age and risk factors indicate the need to begin taking a statin at this time
Delay conception until her HbA1c is as close to normal as possible, if this can be safely achieved

question: A 25-year-old woman pregnant at 15 weeks presents to the clinic complaining of palpitation, tremor and diarrhea for the last 3 weeks. On examination, she looks anxious, she has graves ophthalmopathy and goiter. Other systemic examination are unremarkable. Diagnosis of grave's disease was confirmed but she is refusing to start any treatment while she is pregnant (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/65 mmHg Heart rate 125 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.6 °C BMI 20 kg/m2 Test Result Normal Values Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone < 0.01 0.4 - 5.0 U/mL Triiodothyronine (T3 free serum) 10.0 3.5 - 6.5 pmol/L Thyroxine (T4 free serum) 35.0 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate action?
choices: Agree with her opinion and discharge her from the clinic
Call her husband and force her to start the treatment
Give her follow up after 2 months and repeat her thyroid function test
Explain clearly the risk for her and the fetus and try to convince her to start the treatment Immediately

question: A 45-year-old man presented to the clinic with large thyroid nodule otherwise asymptomatic, that was proven to be papillary thyroid carcinoma. The physician is planning to send him for total thyroidectomy but the patient is afraid from the surgical complication. The treating physician needs to create a lasting impression at the end of the consultation. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?
choices: Patient's agreement for referral is not required
Avoid discussing the serious surgical complications
Briefly explain the action plan with possible expected and unexpected outcome

question: A 22-year-old man developed traumatic paraplegia secondary to a road traffic accident about 8 months ago, requiring prolonged immobilization. His general physical and systemic examination were unremarkable and intact PTH levels (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Calcium 2.75 2.15-2.62 mmol/L Phosphate, inorganic 0.9 0.82-1.51 mmol/L Parathyroid hormone 1.0 1.1-5.3 pmol/L Which of the following is the most probable underlying aetiology for his hypercalcaemia?

A 40-year-old man was referred to the endocrine clinic with symptoms of reduced libido and lack of energy for the last 10 months. On examination, he had normal general physical and systemic examination (see lab results and report). BMI 40 kg/m2 Test Result Normal Values Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 0.3 0.4 - 5.0 wU/mL. Thyroxine (T4 free serum) 7.5 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Follicle-stimulating hormone 2.5 5-20 IU/L (Follicular phase) 15-35 IU/L (Mid cycle peak) 5-15 IU/L (Luteal phase) 50-100 IU/L (Postmenopausal women) 5-20 IU/L (men) Testosterone 8.0 10.4-41.6 mol/L (Male) 0.7-2.8 nmol/L (Female) Luteinizing hormone 1.3 3-15 U/L (Male) 5-22 U/L (Follicular phase) 5-22 U/L (Luteal phase) 30-250 U/L (ovulatory phase) > 30 U/L (Postmenopausal) Prolactin 450 < 652 pmol/L (Male) < 870 pmol/L (Female) MRI brain: Showed 2.5 cm pituitary adenoma. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-year-old boy was referred to the Endocrine Clinic with features of short height and weight gain. On examination, he had increased BMI and central adiposity together with purple striae on lower abdomen (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values ACTH 20 2-11 pmol/L Cortisol 8 a.m. 600 138-635 mol/L Cortisol 4 p.m. 550 83-441 mol/L Cortisol 1 hr after cosyntropin > 500 > 498 mol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in his management?

A 25-year-old man was referred to the Endocrine Clinic with a recent history of fragility fracture. He had no significant past medical history and was on no medication. On examination, he had sparse facial and axillary hair growth. His systemic examination was unremarkable. BMI 23 kg/m2 Which of the following investigations useful in establishing the aetiology of his fragility fractures?

A 40-year-old man was incidentally detected to have a benign 2.0-cm right adrenal adenoma on CT of the abdomen, which was done to evaluate his symptom of abdominal pain. On examination, he had unremarkable general physical and systemic examination. Blood pressure 130/70 mmHg, BMI 26 kq/m2 Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
choices: Dexamethasone suppression test (overnight) and urinary metanephrines

question: A 35-year-old man was found to have a 5.5-cm left adrenal mass with irregular borders and a density of > 10 HU on non-contrast CT of the abdomen. On contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen, there is <30% contrast wash out at 15 minutes. In view of the suspicious radiological features of the mass, the patient was referred to the endocrine surgical team for an elective adrenalectomy. Which of the following investigations should be done prior to an elective adrenalectomy?
choices: Aldosterone to plasma renin activity ratio

question: A 30-year-old woman presents with recurrent attacks of dyspnea and cough when exposed to dust and perfumes. Physical examination is normal except for mild expiratory wheeze on lung auscultation (see report). Spirometry: Reversible bronchospasm. Which of the following is most appropriate to initiate at this stage?

A 60-year-old man with a history of 20-pack-year smoking presents with exertional dyspnea and productive cough for 3 months. He had similar attack last year. On examination, he has central cyanosis and expiratory wheeze on lung auscultation (see lab resuits) Test Result Normal Values ABG HCO3- 36 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 7.7 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.35 7.36-7.45 ABG P02 8.4 10.6-14.2 kPa Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old man heavy smoker, presents with left sided chest pain and hemoptysis for 2 days. Recently his son has noticed change in the quality of his father's voice. On examination, he has early digital clubbing and both of his wrists are painful and tender. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 85 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 92 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
In a patient with acute asthmatic attack, which of the following is the most recommended tool to assess the response to therapy?

A 65-year-old smoker is being evaluated for pleural effusion. He has cough, dyspnea and hemoptysis. On examination, signs of massive pleural effusion are present on right side but the trachea and apex beat are not shifted. Which of the following explains these clinical findings?

A 45-year-old man is diagnosed to have pulmonary tuberculosis for which he was started on 4 anti-tuberculous drugs 2 months ago. During routine follow up, his blood work shows hyperuricemia (see lab result). Test Result Normal Values Uric acid 600 200-410 mol/L (Male) 140-360 mol/L (Female) What anti-TB drug is responsible for this finding?

A 32-year-old man is seen in the clinic for evaluation of primary infertility. Past medical history is significant for recurrent sinusitis. Sperm analysis shows normal number of sperms, but they are immotile (see report). Chest radiography: shows situs inversus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department complaining of progressive dyspnea over 5 days. Past medical history is significant for road traffic accident 2 week ago. Lung auscultation revealed absent breath sounds in the right side (see image and lab results). Blood pressure 100/70 mmH Heart rate 90 /min Respiratory rate 24 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 90 % Test Result Normal Values Hb 90 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) WBC 6 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A male farmer with chronic liver disease secondary to repeated infections of schistosoma mansoni complains of progressive dyspnea. Examination revealed elevated JVP, clear lung fields and left parasternal heave. What is the likely complication that has occurred?

A 45-year-old man presents with 5-year history of cough, productive of large volume of sputum associated with dyspnea and hemoptysis. On examination, he has clubbing and course crackles in the right base. Which of the following tests has the highest diagnostic value?
A 50-year-old woman with pulmonary hypertension is being evaluated for a possibility of chronic thromboembolic disease. Which of the following investigations has the highest diagnostic value?
Which of the following drugs is a leukotriene receptor antagonist?
According to the World Health Organization classification of pulmonary hypertension, which of the following conditions falls under group 3?

A 55-year-old man presents with progressive dyspnea and cough for 6 weeks. He is a heavy smoker. 2 weeks ago, he started having headaches and noticed swelling of his face. Physical examination reveals prominent non-pulsating neck veins, puffiness of the face and edema of the upper limbs (see report). Chest X-ray: Shows a prominence of the right hilum. Which of the following types of lung cancer is the most commonly associated with this clinical presentation?

An asymptomatic 60-year-old man, non-smoker presents for a routine annual physical check-up. A chest X-ray showed an opacity, which is less than 3 cm in the left upper lobe. which of the following is the next best step in the management?

A 55-year old man with stable COPD, presents with sudden onset left-sided pleuritic chest pain and exertional dyspnea. On examination, he is not in distress. the trachea is central and breath sounds are equal in both sides with occasional mild expiratory wheezes (see report). Blood pressure 130/70 mmHg Heart rate 80 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 93 % Chest X-ray: Shows a left sided pneumothorax measuring 2 cm between the lung and chest wall. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 20-year-old woman presents to the Out-Patient Department with mild dyspnea, malaise, low-grade fever and arthralgia. Physical examination showed tender erythematous nodules measuring 2-3 cm in both shins. Chest auscultation revealed fine basal crackles. Which of the following is the next best action in management?
Which of the following is the best oxygen delivery system in a patient with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease?

A 65-year-old man known to have COPD presented to the Emergency Department with increasing dyspnea, cough, expectoration and fever. Initial assessment revealed fully conscious patient with mild distress, central cyanosis and bilateral wheezing on chest auscultation. The patient was started on high flow oxygen and salbutamol nebulizer but 1 hour later, his level of consciousness is reduced (see lab result) Test Result Normal Values ABG HCO3. 36 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 9 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.18 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 15 10.6-14.2 kPa Which of the following is the best initial step in management?

A 30-year-old postpartum woman is admitted to the General Ward with diagnosis of right leg DVT. She was started on enoxaparin 80 mg bid, but in the same day of admission, she developed sudden onset dyspnea and right pleuritic chest pain. On examination, she was dyspneic and apprehensive. Heart sounds showed loud P2 and lungs were clear to auscultation (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 125/70 mmHg Heart rate 100 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Test Result Normal Values ABG HCO3- 22 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 4.2 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.48 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 12 10.6-14.2 kPa Spiral CT chest: Thrombus in the right lower pulmonary artery. Which of the following is the most appropriate step in management?

A 40-year-old man with paraplegia following road traffic accident one year ago is brought to the Emergency Department because of sudden onset dyspnea and chest pain. On examination, he is in severe distress and cyanosed. He has left parasternal heave and loud P2. Chest is clear to auscultation (see lab results and reports). Blood pressure 80/55 mmHg Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 30 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 86 % Test Result Normal Values ABG HCO3- 22 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 4.2 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.4 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 8.6 10.6-14.2 kPa Echocardiogram: Dilated right ventricle with pulmonary artery pressure of 55 mmHg. Venous Doppler: Confirmed DVT in the left leg extending to the thigh. Which of the following is the best line of management?

A 50-year-old woman presented with fever, dyspnea and weight loss. Physical examination showed evidence of pleural effusion in the left hemithorax (see report). Pleural fluid analysis: Shows exudative fluid with high gamma interferon level. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old man with COPD, presented with increasing dyspnea, cough and bilateral lower limb swelling. Physical examination showed elevated JVP, hepatomegaly and pitting edema in both lower limbs. Chest auscultation revealed scattered rhonchi in both sides. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
choices: High resolution CT scan of chest

question: In a patient with COPD and cor pulmonale, which of the following improves survival?

A 30-year-old woman is evaluated for a 6-month history of recurrent dyspnea, cough, and wheezing. She is awakened with asthma symptoms 6-8 nights a month. Her current medication is salbutamol inhaler. On examination, there are wheezes in both lung fields. Which of the following is the most appropriate next best step in management?
choices: Inhaled budesonide and inhaled albuterol as needed

question: A 30-year-old woman complains of recurrent attacks of sudden onset dyspnea, chest and throat tightness. Inhaled salbutamol is of little help; however, her symptoms improves suddenly. On examination, she is found to have inspiratory wheeze during dyspnea spells. which of the following is the likely cause of symptoms?

A 55-year-old obese non-smoker man with hypertension presents with exertional dyspnea for 2 years. His wife stated that he is uncomfortable while sleeping at night and produces loud snores. Examination revealed central cyanosis, suffused conjunctivae and clear chest. BMI 40 kg/m2 Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

BMI 40 kg/m2 Test Result Normal Values ABG HCO3- 38 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 6.9 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.38 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 9 10.6-14.2 ka Which of the following is the best treatment after polysomnography?

A 60-year-old man known to have COPD refused the advice to stop smoking. What is the best statement should be given to him during a communication session?
choices: "You better stop smoking otherwise you will die"
'We will do everything to help you stop smoking"
"We have to talk to your family about this refusal"
"If you don't stop smoking we will stop seeing you in the clinic"

question: A 56-year-old man who has chronic productive cough underwent a CT chest, which was consistent with bronchiectasis. He came today to discuss his disease. Which of the following would convey the diagnostic information to him?
choices: Read to him the CT report
Show him the chest X-ray film
Inform him that he has bronchiectasis
Tell him that his air tubules are inflamed and damaged

question: A young patient has poorly controlled asthma and her doctor decided to start her on oral steroids. She is uncomfortable about that decision. When counselling this patient, what is the most important communication aspect should be addressed?
choices: The scientific basis of using steroids

question: A 74-year-old man, who smokes for 40 years, underwent a CT chest, which showed a large lung mass.Which of the following is the most appropriate way to break the bad news?
choices: Avoid wasting time and tell him directly that he has lung cancer
Inform him that this is nothing to worry about
Inform him that he should stop smoking
Deliver the information in small steps

question: A patient with interstitial lung disease has repeated admissions for pneumonia. His son is worried about antibiotics induced diarrhoea. Which of the following is the most appropriate way to address this situation?
choices: Tell him that the diarrhea is not serious
Stress that the hospital infection control policy will be implemented
Agree with him that the antibiotics should be stopped
Apologize for repeatedly using antibiotics to treat his father

question: A 28-year-old man, who is a known drug addict, is found in deep coma and cyanosed. Blood pressure 100/55 mmH Heart rate 55 /min Respiratory rate 8 /min Oxygen saturation 85 % Which of the following is the most important initial management?
choices: Obtain detailed history from the family

question: A 53-year-old man with liver cirrhosis presents with several episodes of vomiting of blood and black tarry stool. Blood pressure: Supine 105/60 mmH Sitting 85/50 mmHg Heart rate: Supine 90 /min Sitting 110 /min Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
choices: Intravenous infusion of H2 receptor antagonists

A 40-year-old woman is admitted with diagnosis of Guillain Barre Syndrome. Which of the following would be the most appropriate method for monitoring ventilatory impairment?

A 45-year old man is just admitted to the Critical Care Unit with polytrauma following road traffic accident because of hypotension. He is sedated and mechanically ventilated. Blood pressure 85/55 mmHg Heart rate 110 /min Temperature 36.0 °C Oxygen saturation 100 % Central venous pressure: Right atrial pressure 15 mmHg Chest radiograph: Cardiomegaly and fractured sternum. A 35-year-old man is evaluated in the Orthopedic Ward because of dyspnea, tachycardia and confusion. The patient had fractured left femur for which he undergone internal fixation 2-days ago. A 16-year-old boy presents with a several days history of progressive arm and leg weakness. No diplopia or loss of sphincter control. He has been well except for an upper respiratory infection 2 weeks ago. On examination, his breathing is slow and shallow. His heart rate and blood pressure are fluctuant. There is symmetrical weakness of the face and all four extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are absent, and sensations are intact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man presents with an 8-week history of severe headache. The headaches have occurred at the same time each day, about 2 a.m. and last around 30 minutes. Headaches are accompanied by lacrimation and redness of the right eye. Which of the following is the best to prevent this type of headache?

A 55-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension complains of pain in the right eve and double vision when looking to the left. Fundoscopy and other cranial nerve are normal as well as the rest of neurological examination of the upper and lower limbs.Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?

An 18-year-old boy known to have grand mal epilepsy since childhood is brought to the Emergency Department after having repeated tonic-clonic seizures at home. After oxygenation and securing the airway, which of the following intravenous drugs should be administered?
In a patient with Guillain Barre Syndrome, which of the following is the best treatment option?

A 30-year-old woman presents with pain in the right eye associated progressive visual loss over 2 days. She also reported a numbness in the left side of the face and weakness in both lower limbs. Physical examination revealed reduced visual acuity, loss of direct light reflex with preserved indirect light reflex in the right eye. Lower limbs examination showed weakness, clasp knife rigidity, hyperrefiexia in both knee and ankle jerks. There is loss of all modalities of sensation in both lower limbs. An elderly patient sustained a major stroke and he is intubated in the intensive Care Unit. However, even he was in a very critical state, he managed to write in the bed clothes that he wants to die in peace. Few days later, he passed away without resuscitation according to what he wrote. His son was very angry and said that his father had no mental capacity to decide. What is the most appropriate stand when dealing with this situation?
choices: Find out whether the son is the real next of kin
Tell the son that in anyway his father would have never made it
Inform the son that the doctors respected the wish of your father

question: A young woman is diagnosed to have multiple sclerosis. She went through an emotional breakdown during breaking bad news. Which of the following is the most appropriate way to express empathy?
choices: "I share you your feelings and will support you"
"Pull yourself up and follow our instructions"
"I am very sorry for what happened"
"Do not worry, you will be fine"

(Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) ESR 85 2-10 mm/h (Male) 3-15 mm/h (Female) Which of the following is expected feature on physical examination?

A 60-year-old man with diabetes presented with progressive ascites, fever and weight loss for 2-months. Paracentesis revealed low serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old man with HBV cirrhosis presents with increasing abdominal girth, lower limb edema, and 10 kg weight gain over the last 3 months. choices: Colitis limited to the most distal 15 cm of colon

question: A previously healthy 22-year-old woman reports 3-month history of frequent bloody bowel movements with mucus and occasional right hip pain. (Male) 120-160 q/L (Female) MCV 72 80-95 fl Stool analysis: Shows many RBCs and few WBCs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman presents with abdominal pain, bloating and weight loss. A young woman who is known to have pan ulcerative colitis is admitted for a severe relapse. Since there was no response to medical treatment, surgery is decided. The patient is very sceptical about surgery and requested more information. What is the appropriate way to address her concerns?
choices: Tell her that she will die if surgery is not performed
Discard her concerns as unfounded and push her for surgery
Inform her that surgery will leave her with a colostomy bag

question: A 52-year-old man, who has been medically treated as peptic ulcer for a long time, underwent upper endoscopy, which showed a malignant ulcer. During the visit, he started blaming his primary physician and wanted to file a complaint. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?
choices: Agree that it is his right to do so
Take a neutral stand in this issue
Inform him that his doctor did what he could do

choices: Disclose the result to his emplover
Request the social worker to inform his wife
Report to the infection control unit in the hospital

question: A 60-year-old man presented with high-grade fever and left pleuritic chest pain. On examination, he has early clubbing and evidence of moderate pleural effusion in the left side of the chest. Pleural fluid analysis revealed pH of 7,0. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension is admitted with extensive anterior ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). had successful angioplasty and stenting to left anterior descending artery. Aspirin, clopidogrel, bisoprolol and enalapril were started (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Cholesterol (HDL) 1.0 > 1.03 mmol/L Cholesterol (LDL) 3.36 <3.36 mmol/L Total Cholesterol 5.0 <5.1 mmol/L Triglycendes 2.2 <2.16 mmol/L Which of the following is recommended?

A 55-year-old man with diabetes presented to the Cardiology Clinic with vague chest pain with exertion for 2 months (see report). Electrocardiogram: Normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 60-year-old man with poorly controlled hypertension presents with exertional dyspnea and occasional paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. No chest pain or palpitation. On examination, he is comfortable at rest; the JVP is 3 cm above sternal border, loud A2 and left ventricular $4, no murmur (see reports). Blood pressure 160/100 mmH Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Oxygen saturation 95 % Electrocardiogram: Shows sinus rhythm and left ventricular hypertrophy. Echocardiogram: Normal cardiac chambers size, concentric left ventricular hypertrophy and normal left ventricular ejection fraction. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man is found to have cardiomegaly on chest X-ray during pre-employment check-up. He denies chest pain, dyspnea, orthopnea or PND. Physical examination unremarkable (see reports). Blood pressure 120/80 mg Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Electrocardiogram: Normal. Echocardiogram: Dilated left ventricle with ejection fraction of 40%. Which of the following is the best management?

A 45-year-old man with previous history of rheumatic heart disease presents with worsening dyspnea, orthopnea and PND. Physical examination shows holosystolic murmur in the apex and bibasilar crackles on lung auscultation. His symptoms improved with furosemide, spironolactone, enalapril and carvedilol (see report). Echocardiogram: Showed mildly dilated left ventricle, LVEF 45% and severe rheumatic mitral regurgitation. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

A 70-year-old man is found to have ejection systolic murmur in the aortic area during routine medical check-up. He denied symptoms of dyspnea, chest pain or syncope. Physical examination revealed slow raising carotid pulsation; normal JVP and normal lung auscultation (see reports). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Electrocardiogram: Normal sinus rhythm with LVH. Echocardiogram: Shows concentric LVH, normal ejection fraction and severely stenosed aortic valve. Which of the following is the next step in management?

A 30-year-old woman with history of rheumatic heart disease since childhood presented with exertional dyspnea and occasional paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical examination showed JVP of 5 cm above sternal angle, loud S1, loud P2 and mid diastolic rumbling murmur in the apex. Fine basal crackles are present on lung auscultation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old man presents with abdominal distension dyspnea and orthopnea. The JVP is markedly elevated and fails to descend during inspiration. Lower limbs showed massive pitting edema up to the thighs. Heart sounds are normal. There are bibasilar crackles on lung auscultation. Abdominal examination showed hepatomegaly and positive shifting dullness (see report). Echocardiogram: Both atria are dilated. Left and right ventricles are normal in size and LVEF is 60%. No valve lesions. Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

An 18-year-old boy presents with recurrent syncope with exercise. Physical examination showed normal JVP, jerky carotid pulsations and thrusting apex. There is an ejection systolic murmur, which is best heard in the left parasternal area that increases in intensity with standing and reduced during handgrip (see report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Electrocardiogram: Shows left ventricular hypertrophy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A young man with diagnosis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy presented with recurrent exertional chest pain and syncope. Which of the following is the best management?

A 65-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension, presented with retrosternal chest pain at rest for 3 hours. Physical examination is normal except for $4 gallop (see lab result and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Oxygen saturation 95 % Test Result Normal Values Troponin 10 < 0.2 pg/L Electrocardiogram: T-wave inversion in leads V2-V5. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension is admitted to the Coronary Care Unit with diagnosis of unstable angina. Physical examination is normal except for S4 gallop. Aspirin, bisoprolol, enoxaparn, atorvastatin and nitrate are started (see lab result and reports). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Test Result Normal Values Troponin .001 < 0.2 pg/L Electrocardiogram: Showed ST depression in leads II, III, AVF. Echocardiogram: Normal. What additional medication is indicated?

A 30-year-old man presents with burning retrosternal chest pain associated with dyspnea. His history is significant only for common cold 2 weeks ago (see image). Which of the following clinical signs is likely to be present?

A 70-year-old man presents with dyspnea, fatigue and presyncope. On examination, the JVP showed Cannon a-wave and variations in the intensity of the first heart sound (see image). Which of the following is the definitive treatment?

A 64-year-old woman with advanced breast cancer complains of dyspnea on exertion. On examination, her systolic blood pressure is noted to markedly decrease during inspiration. Heart sounds are distant to auscultation. Chest is clear (see report). Blood pressure 95/65 mmH, Heart rate 100 /min, Respiratory rate 24 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C, Oxygen saturation 95 % Chest x-ray: Marked cardiomegaly with clear lung fields. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman with diabetes and hypercholesterolemia presents to the Emergency Department with chest tightness associated with sweating and nausea of 4-hour duration. Physical examination showed elevated JVP, which increases further during inspiration, S4 gallop and clear lung fields on chest auscultation. Aspirin and clopidogrel were given. Results of cardiac enzymes are pending (see image). Blood pressure 90/55 mmH Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Oxygen saturation 95 % Which of the following immediate action should be taken?

A 25-year-old woman presented with dyspnea and cyanosis. Physical examination revealed elevated JVP with predominant a-wave and left parasternal heave. There is an ejection systolic murmur best heard in the left second intercostal space that increases in intensity during inspiration. An ejection click is also heard in the same area Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old man is admitted for stomach resection for gastric cancer. On the 4TH postoperative day. the patient developed retrosternal chest pain accompanied with dyspnea and perfuse sweating. Physical examination is remarkable only for S4. Aspirin, clopidogrel and nitrate were administered (see report) Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Respiratory rate 18 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Electrocardiogram: Shows ST elevation in leads V2-V5. Which of the following is the most appropriate step in management?

A 70-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes and aortic sclerosis discovered to have atrial fibrillation on routine health check-up. He denies dyspnea, chest pain or palpitations. Which of the following drugs is recommended to prevent systemic embolization?

A 22-year-old woman presents with retrosternal burning chest pain, which is worse during breathing and coughing. Precordial auscultation showed an added sound of 3 components; systolic, diastolic and presystolic (see image). Which of the following is the best initial treatment?
In a patient with heart failure due to dilated cardiomyopathy presenting with fast atrial fibrillation, which of the following drugs is the most appropriate to control the heart rate?

A 40-year-old man is admitted with palpitations of 4-hour duration. He had similar attack a month ago but did not seek medical advice. His initial electrocardiogram showed atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular rate. He subsequently converted to sinus rhythm. Which of the following drugs is the most appropriate to maintain sinus rhythm?

An 18-year-old girl is recently diagnosed to have rheumatic fever with carditis. Echocardiogram showed mild mitral stenosis with mild regurgitation. To what age the rheumatic fever prophylaxis is recommended?
Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for thrombolvtic therapy?
choices: Blood pressure at presentation of 180/110 mmH

question: A 28-year-old woman presents to the Cardiology Outpatient Department with recurrent palpitations for the last 6 months. She describes the palpitations as fast heartbeat, which starts and ends suddenly. Each attack lasts 5-10 min. No associated chest pain, dyspnea, syncope or presyncope (see lab result and report). Test Result Normal Values Hb 132 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 3.8 0.4 - 5.0 jU/mL. Electrocardiogram: Normal sinus rhythm with rate of 70/min. Which of the following is the best next investigation?

An elderly patient is admitted with diagnosis of unstable angina. He is known to have atrial fibrillation and taking warfarin. The attending resident administered heparin but did not check the INR, which came back as 6.8. The patient developed bleeding from the gums and hematuria. His son is upset, and he requests an explanation. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?
choices: Say that you are sorry for what happened and request him to calm down
Apologize and reassure him that you will start an investigation
Tell him that this is an expected side effect of the drug
Inform him that the situation is under control

question: A 60-year-old man with hypertension and diabetes undergone coronary angiogram, which showed 3-vessel disease requiring coronary bypass surgery. The patient refused surgery. Being the resident with the team, what is the appropriate communication tool to be used?
choices: Tell the son to speak to the patient
Respect autonomy and continue medical treatment
Apply the counselling in the presence of the consultant

question: A patient who presented with heart failure had an echocardiogram, which showed severe rheumatic mitral regurgitation requiring valve replacement. He is waiting to know the result. Which of the following is the most appropriate way to break the news?
choices: Avoid asking him about what he already knows
Tell him all the details from the beginning
Deliver the information in small steps

question: A 53-year-old widow with dilated cardiomyopathy presented to the Cardiology Clinic with decompensated heart failure. She lives alone, has no insurance and cannot afford the cost of medications. During counselling, which of the following is the most appropriate plan?
choices: Arrange for a charity organization to help her financially
Involve the social worker and the hospital support system
Refer her to the Emergency Department
Advise her to avoid salt and stop smoking

question: A 79-year-old man with multiple co-morbidities is hospitalized for dissecting aneurysm and needs urgent surgery. He lives alone and he has no written will or advanced directive. His condition is very critical in the ICU. What is the best way to arrange the consent for surgery?
choices: The attending medical team should sign the consent form
The social worker is asked to complete the consent form
Proceed for emergency and delay the consent

question: A 38-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department with 5-day history of fever and a productive cough (see lab results and reports) Blood pressure 100/65 mHg Temperature 39 °C Test Result Normal Values WBC 12 4.5-10.5 x 109/L ESR 26 2-10 mm/h (Male) 3-15 mm/h (Female) Chest X-ray: Right middle lobe infiltrate. Sputum culture: Pending. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate therapy?

A 27-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department with 2-days history of confusion and 5-hours history of seizures. Positive history of multiple unprotected sexual contact for the last 6 years. On examination, he was disoriented to time; place and person (see lab results and report. Temperature 39 °C Test Result Normal Values WBC 1.3 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Serum Cryptococcal Antigen: Positive. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic test?
A 22-year-old man recently diagnosed with HIV presented to the clinic for counselling. Whom should he disclose his HIV status to?
A 53-year-old man recently diagnosed with HIV came to the clinic for counselling. Who should be offered HIV testing?

A 69-year-old man known to have diabetes mellitus, presented to Emergency department with 4-day history of productive cough and tachypnea. On examination, oriented to time place and person. Chest exam revealed right lower lobe crepitation (see lab results and report). Respiratory rate 23 /min Temperature 38.5 °C Test Result Normal Values WBC 12 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Urea 5 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Chest X-Ray: Right lower lobe intiltrate. Which of the following is the most appropriate management approach?
choices: Admit to general ward and start IV antibiotics
Admit to Intensive care unit and start IV antibiotics
Start oral antibiotics and observe in Emergency Room for 24 hours
Start oral antibiotics and see in outpatient clinic in 7-days

question: A 70-year-old woman known to have hypertension on medication. Presented to the Emergency Department with 4-days history of productive cough, shortness of breath and tachypnea. Chest exam, right lobe zone crepitation. Temperature 38.5 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate next diagnostic test to confirm the diagnosis?

A 54-year-old man known to have diabetes and hypertension presented to Emergency Department with 9-days history of cough, headache, shortness of breath and fever. Cough was productive of white sputum, which has become yellowish lately. On chest examination, wheezing, and right side crepitation (see lab results and reports). Temperature 38 °C Test Result Normal Values Reticulocyte 8 0.2-1.2 % WBC 12 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Cold agglutinin titre: 1:256 Chest X-Ray: Bilateral shadowing both lungs with more density on the right middle lobe. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman referred to the clinic with 3-weeks history of generalized fatigability, malaise, arthralgia, back pain and fever. Positive history of raw milk ingestion. Abdominal examination, mild hepato-splenomegaly (see lab results and report). Temperature 39 °C Test Result Normal Values Hb 10.5 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 120 150-400 x 109/L Blood culture: Gram negative cocco-bacilli. Which of the following is the first line in treatment option?

A 28-year-old woman referred to the clinic with 3-week history of generalized fatigability. malaise, arthralgia, back pain and fever. Positive history of raw milk ingestion. Abdominal examination, mild hepato-splenomegaly (see lab results and reports). Temperature 38.5 °C Test Result Normal Values Hb 10.5 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 120 150-400 x 109/L Blood culture: Gram negative cocco-bacilli MRI of the back: Sacroiliac joint spondylitis. Which of the following is the optimal duration of therapy?

A 45-year-old housemaid from Southeast Asia, recently came to Saudi Arabia, presented to the Emergency Department with 2-weeks history of productive cough and shortness of breath. Positive history of hemoptysis. Chest exam showed right upper zone crepitations (see lab results and report. Temperature 38.5 °C Test Result Normal Values WBC 14 4.5-10.5 x 109/L ESR 73 2-10 mm/h (Male) 3-15 mm/h (Female) Chest X-Ray: Right upper lobe infiltrate and cavitation. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 45-year-old man admitted to the hospital with history of productive cough and shortness of breath. He was found to have cavitatory pulmonary tuberculosis (TB. He was started on 4 anti-TB drugs. Few days later, he noticed that the urine color is red. Detailed history revealed family history of urethral stones (see lab resuits). Test Result Normal Values Hb 11 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 110 150-400 x 109/L Which of the following is the most likely cause of his new symptom?

A 45-year-old man admitted to the hospital with history of productive cough and shortness of breath. He was found to have positive acid fast bacilli (AFB) in sputum. He was started on isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol. He came back to the clinic for follow up after 3-weeks. Cough was better and no other symptoms (see lab results) Admission lab results: Test Result Normal Values Total bilirubin 5 3.5-16.5 mol/L Aspartate aminotransferase 28 12-40 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase 32 5-40 IU/L ESR 75 2-10 mm/h (Male) 3-15 mm/h (Female) Follow-up lab results: Test Result Normal Values Total bilirubin 0.7 3.5-16.5 mol/L Aspartate aminotransferase 75 12-40 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase 80 5-40 IU/L ESR 35 2-10 mm/h (Male) 3-15 mm/h (Female) Sputum AB Negative Which of the following is the best management approach?
choices: Continue anti-TB and repeat LFT in 1 week
Stop all anti-TB and repeat LFT in 1 weeks
Stop pyrazinamide and repeat LFT in 2 weeks
Stop isoniazid and rifampin and repeat LFT in 2 weeks

question: A 60-year-old man known to have hypertension and post aortic valve replacement on lisinopril 20 mg. amlodipine 5 mg and warfarin 3 mg once daily. He was admitted to the hospital with history of productive cough and shortness of breath, and was found to have positive acid fast bacilli (AFB) in sputum. First line four anti-TB drugs were started. Which of the following regarding medications should be done?
choices: Lisinopril dose needs to be decreased

question: A 60-year-old man from India presented to the Emergency Department with headache and low-grade fever for 3-weeks. The headache became worse over the last 2-days and was associated with vomiting. In the emergency room, he developed generalized seizures (see lab results and reports), Test Result Normal Values WBC 19 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Pressure 280 200-250 mmH20 (Male) 300-400 mmH20 (Female) Cells 380 0-3 /ML Total protein (Men) 3 0.22-0.33 g/L Glucose 1.2 2.50-3.89 mmol/L CSF differential WBC count: 73% lymphocytes and 13 % neutrophils. CSF culture: Pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 53-year-old woman known diabetic, hypertensive and cardiac arrhythmia on amiodarone, presented to Emergency Department with 3-days history of progressive redness and pain on her right leg. Examination showed a sharply demarcated red lesion, which was tender with no ulcer, Temperature 38.8 °C. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 53-year-old woman known diabetic presented to the Emergency Department with 5-days history of progressive redness and pain on her right thigh. On examination, right thigh showed 15 cm red lesion, which was tender with no uicer (see report). Temperature 38.3 °C Ultrasound: Showed inflammatory changes and 10 x 8 cm deep abscess collection. Which of the following is the best management approach?
choices: Admit to ward and start IV antibiotics
Admit to ICU and start IV antibiotics
Discharge home on oral antibiotics with 1-week follow up
Admit to ward, start IV antibiotics, and surgical consultation

question: A 53-year-old woman recently returned from Egypt, known diabetic, presented to the Emergency Department with 3-days history of progressive redness and pain on her right shin. Positive history of allergy to penicillin. On examination, right leg has red lesion, which was tender with no ulcer. She was started on oral antibiotics. Next day she complained of abdominal pain, watery diarrhoea and fever. Temperature 37.8 °C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old woman known diabetic for the last 20-years on insulin, presented to the Emergency Department with 3-days history of right knee pain and swelling. Right knee examination revealed, red, swollen and tender with severely limited range of movement. Other joints were normal (see lab result and report). Temperature 39 °C Test Result Normal Values WBC 17 4.5-10.5 × 109/L Synovial fluid: WBC: 55.000 Crystals: Pending Culture: Negative Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with 3-days history of generalized body aches, sore throat, runny nose, productive cough and shortness of breath. Chest exam shows right lung crepitations. The patient was admitted and according to the results of throat swab was started on oseltamivir (see report). Temperature 39 °C. Chest X-Ray: Right middle lobe infiltrate. Which of the following isolation precautions should be considered?

A 33-year-old woman presents with headache and myalgia for 5 days. 2 days ago, she started to have fever and noticed a skin rash on her face. She returned from Jeddah 10-days ago (see lab resuits). Test Result Normal Values Hb 8 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 80 150-400 x 109/L Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 27-year-old soldier going to a military mission at the Southern border of Saudi Arabia. His medical history is insignificant apart from a positive history of depression, which is controlled by medication. He came for counselling regarding malaria prevention. Which of the following is the best malaria chemoprophylaxis regimen?

A 30-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with history of fever and headache. He recently came from a trip to Sudan, where he stayed there for 10-days. Abdominal examination, palpable spleen 3 cm below costal margin (see lab results). Temperature 40 °C Test Result Normal Values Hb 9 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 90 150-400 x 109/L Aspartate aminotransferase 88 12-40 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase 94 5-40 IU/L Which of the following is the first line treatment option?

A 45-year-old man, heavy smoker, presents to the Emergency Department with 5-days history of fever and skin rash and 3-days of dyspnea and dry cough. Skin examination shows vesicular lesions over the truck and extremities, some of the lesions were crusted. Chest examination shows bilateral crepitation's (see report). Respiratory rate 28/min Temperature 39 °C Oxygen saturation 82 % Chest X-Ray: Diffuse bilateral infiltrate. Which of the following is the most appropriate intravenous treatment option?

A 22-year-old man recently returned from Umrah, presents to Emergency Department with 1-day history of fever and headache. Upon arrival to the Emergency Department, he started to have seizures on the right extremities. On examination, positive Kering sign (see lab results and report). Temperature 39 °C Test Result Normal Values Cells 380 0-3 /pL Total protein (Men) 1.2 0.22-0.33 g/L CSF analysis: WBC differential count: 87% neutrophils and 5% lymphocytes. Which of the following is the most appropriate intravenous treatment option?

A 22-year-old man presents to Emergency Department with 4-days history of fever, headache and confusion. On examination, Kemig's sign is present (see lab results and reports). Temperature 39 °C Test Result Normal Values Cells 380 0-3 /pL Total protein (Men) 0.8 0.22-0.33 g/L Glucose 3.7 2.50-3.89 mmol/L CSF analysis: WBC differential count: 5% neutrophil and 90% lymphocytes. CSF Culture: Pending. Which of the following is the most appropriate intravenous treatment option?

A 22-year-old man recently returned from Hal, presents to Emergency Department with 1-day history of fever and headache. On examination, Kerig's sign is present. Skin examination showed petechial rash on extremities and trunk (see lab results and report). Temperature 39 °C Test Result Normal Values Cells 380 0-3 /pL Total protein (Men) 0.9 0.22-0.33 g/L Glucose 1.2 2.50-3.89 mmol/L CSF analysis: WBC differential: 87% neutrophils and 5% lymphocytes. Which of the following isolation precautions should be considered?

A 27-year-old man recently returned from Umrah. Presents to Emergency Department with 1- day history of fever and headache. On examination, positive Kernig's sign and petechial rash on extremities and trunk. He was isolated and started on antibiotics (see lab results and report). Temperature 39 °C Test Result Normal Values Cells 380 0-3 /pL Total protein (Men) 0.9 0.22-0.33 g/L Glucose 1.2 2.50-3.89 mmol/L CSF analysis: WBC differential 87 % neutrophil and 5 % lymphocytes. How many hours after starting antibiotics should isolation be discontinued?

A 64-year-old diabetic woman was recently started on hemo-dialysis through a femoral central line. During dialysis, the nurse notices that she is shivering. Detailed history reveals a 3-day history of fever. On examination, central line site was red with pus discharge. Which of the following is the most appropriate management approach?
choices: Withdraw blood culture and start IV antibiotics
Start IV antibiotics and hold dialysis for 3 days
Withdraw blood culture, change the line and resume dialysis
Withdraw blood culture, start antibiotics and remove the line

question: A 64-year-old diabetic woman is receiving hemo-dialysis through a femoral central line. She develops line sepsis. Blood culture grows MRSA (methicillin resistant staphylococcus aureus). She was started on IV vancomycin 1000 mg every 72 hours (to be infused over 20 min). Immediately after starting vancomycin, she started to have flushing, redness and itching over the face, neck and trunk. Which of the following is the most appropriate management approach?
choices: Stop vancomycin and label her allergic to vancomycin
Continue vancomycin but a lower dose
Continue vancomycin but slower infusion rate
Change vancomycin to cefazolin 1000 mg every 24 hours

question: A 38-year-old woman came for routine follow up 2-months after delivery. She has no symptoms and her baby is well and lactating normally. Upon reviewing her labs, a positive urine culture: >100,000 fu/ml E. coli was noticed which was sensitive to trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, ciprofioxacin, and nitrofurantoin. Which of the following is the best treatment option?

A 38-year-old woman, 28-weeks pregnant came for routine follow up. She has no symptoms and her pregnancy is all well. Upon reviewing her labs, a positive urine culture: > 100,000 fu/mi E.coli was found which was sensitive to ciprofioxacin, nitrofurantoin, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole and ceftriaxone Which of the following is the best treatment option?

A 45-year-old diabetic woman presented to Emergency Department with fever, flank pain and dysuria. She is allergic to penicillin. Examination shows flank tenderness (see lab result and report). Temperature 39 °C Test Result Normal Values WBC 17 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Urine culture: > 100.000 cfu/ml E.coli. Which of the following is absolutely contraindicated?

A 45-year-old woman presented to Emergency Department with fever, flank pain and dysuria (see lab result and report). Test Result Normal Values WBC 14 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Urine culture: > 100,000 cfu/mi E.coll Which of the following is the best empirical treatment option?

A 48-year-old diabetic woman presented to Emergency Department with dysuria (see lab result and report). Test Result Normal Values WBC 14 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Creatinine 230 44-115 mol/L Urine culture: > 100,000 cfu/ml E.coli Which of the following medications is contraindicated?

A 62-year-old man presented with 2-weeks history of tiredness, dyspnea and 5-days history of fever. No previous surgical history. Cardiac exam shows pan-systolic murmur at the apex. Hands exam shows splinter hemorrhage on nails. Temperature 38.8 °C Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

A 58-year-old man presented with 2-weeks history of tiredness, dyspnea and 5-days history of fever. No previous surgical history. Cardiac exam shows pan systolic murmur at the apex. Hands exam shows splinter hemorrhage on nails Temperature 38.5 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate empirical therapy?
A 24-year-old woman is 10-weeks pregnant. She has dysuria and is diagnosed with a urinary tract infection. Which of the following antibiotics is contraindicated?

A 22-year-old woman presented to the clinic with 2-months history of polyarthralgia, skin rash, mucosal ulcers and fatigue. Her clinical examinations revealed malar rash over her face and active arthnitis at several joints (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Hb 100 130-170 g/L. (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 100 150-400 x 109/L WBC 3 4.5-10.5 x 109/L ESR 35 2-10 mm/h (Male) 3-15 mm/h (Female) Lupus anticoagulant positive negative Urea 5 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 78 44-115 mol/L C-reactive peptide 5 <8.2 mg/L Complement C3 0.3 0.7-1.5 g/L Complement C4 0.13 0.15-0.45 g/L Which of the following test obtained at this visit is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman presented to the clinic with polyarthralgia, malar rash and mucosal ulcerations for 2-months. Examination revealed active malar rash and arthritis affecting several joints. She has positive anti-nuclear antibody with high titer (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Hb 110 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 280 150-400 x 109/L WBC 10 4.5-10.5 x 109/L ESR 65 2-10 mm/h (Male) 3-15 mm/h (Female) Urea 4 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 60 44-115 mol/L Appearance clear clear Protein absent absent Leukocytes 2 0-3 per high power field Erythrocytes 0 0-2 per high power field Complement C3 0.6 0.7-1.5 g/L Complement C4 0.13 0.15-0.45 g/L Alkaline phosphatase 50 39-117 TU/L Alanine aminotransferase 18 5-40 IU/L Aspartate aminotransferase 20 12-40 IU/L Which of the following is the best treatment option at this time?

A 30-year-old woman presented to the clinic with polyarthralgia, malar rash and mucosal ulcerations for 2-months. Examination revealed active malar rash and arthritis affecting several joints. She has positive anti-nuclear antibody with high titer (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Hb 100 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 90 150-400 × 109/L WBC 3.5 4.5-10.5 x 109/L ESR 60 2-10 mm/h (Male) 3-15 mm/h (Female) Urea 5 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 150 44-115 mol/L Protein 1200 0-150 mg/24 hr Complement C3 0.4 0.7-1.5 g/L Complement C4 0.1 0.15-0.45 g/L Which of the following is the best high dose treatment option at this time?

A 50-year-old man with active rheumatoid arthritis presented to the clinic complaining of polyarthralgia and significant early morning stiffness. His current treatments are methotrexate, prednisone and hydroxychioroquine. Examination revealed active arthritis at several joints (see lab results). A 25-year-old man developed fever, malaise and rash on the palms of his hands as well as on the soles of both feet. 6 weeks earlier, he had a painless ulcer on his penis. Increase the risk of atrophic gastritis

High dose of oral H2 blocker

question: A 44-year-old woman known to have gall bladder stones presented with biliary pain and jaundice. US abdomen confirmed CBD stones. She underwent ERCP for stone extraction. question: A 30-year-old woman with bronchial asthma developed worsening dyspnea and cough following paint inhalation from neighborhood apartment. choices: Nasal continuous positive airway pressure ventilation

question: A patient with poorly controlled bronchial asthma developed hypertension, which of the following antihypertensive medications is contraindicated?

A 40-year-old woman presents with progressive dyspnea, dry cough and reddish nodular skin lesion over both shins. Chest radiograph: Diffuse bilateral interstitial infiltrates with bilateral hilar lymph nodes enlargement. Purified protein derivative (PPD): Negative. A 60-year-old man with post pulmonary tuberculosis bronchiectasis presents with massive hemoptysis. Physical examination shows course crepitations in the right scapular area (see image). Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

choices: Ignore the opinion of the son and give the antibiotics to save the patient
Counsel the son in the presence of the consultants

question: A young woman with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis is diagnosed to have non-specific interstitial lung disease. The physician decided to start her on oral glucocorticoid. choices: Stress the importance of the treatment and give the patient time to decide
Inform the patient that refusing this treatment might cause death
Inform the patient that there is no alternative treatment
Tell the patient that most of the side effects are not serious

question: An elderly patient is diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis and started on anti-TB treatment. He developed jaundice, which progressed to liver failure for which he was admitted to the Critical Care Unit. His son was very angry and decided to complain against the treating team. What is the appropriate response to the son?
choices: Tell him that this incident can happen to anyone
Inform him that the doctors offered the right management
Advise him against complaining as there is no medical error
Calm him down and inform him that this incident will be investigated

question: An elderly patient who has poorly controlled bronchial asthma with repeated admission to the hospital is found to be non-compliant with his medications. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?
choices: Tell the patient that it is not acceptable to disrespect the advice of doctors
As the patient is noncompliant, just keep him in the hospital
Involve the next of kin to help to give his medications as prescribed

question: A 71-year-old man who has been admitted due to clostriduim difficile infection last year.
