A patient with atrial fibrillation is on warfarin 5 mg daily, the latest IN is 7.0 on routine evaluation. There is no evidence of abnormal bleeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?
choices: Continue with same dose of warfarin
Hold warfarin and repeat IN next day

question: A 73-year-old man comes to the Primary Health Care Clinic with severe shortness of breath at night and swelling of the ankles. He has reduced his activity over the past year because of chest pain when he exerts himself. Physical examination confirms crackles over both lungs, enlargement of the liver, and pieng edema of the ankles. ECG, cardiac enzymes and blood electrolytes are normal. Blood pressure 140/90 mmHg Heart rate 95 /min Respiratory rate 24 /min Temperature 36.6° C  Which of the following is the most appropriate to be included in immediate management?

A 70-year-old man, with no past medical history, presents to the Emergency Department 4 hours after the onset of a severe crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the neck and left arm (see report). Electrocardiography: Significant ST-segment elevation in leads I, AVL, V5, and V6. Where is the most likely site of cardiac infarction?

A 60-year-old patient presents to the hospital, complaining of a sudden onset of chest pain radiating to the back. The blood pressure is low in the left arm and the left femoral pulse is not palpable (see reports). Chest X-ray: A left pleural effusion. ECG: Left ventricular hypertrophy. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 46-year-old man recovering from an acute myocardial infarction 10 days ago. He develops a sharp pain behind the sternum which is made worse by coughing. The patient gets relief when sieng forward. On examination, a scratchy superficial sound is heard at the left sternal edge, and heart sounds are muffled. There is ascites and a 2 cm raised JVP is confirmed. Which of the following ECG changes would most likely be found?

A 60-year-old man is admitted to the Coronary Care Unit with an acute myocardial infarction. His hemodynamic parameters 2 hours later are: Blood pressure 80/50 mHg Heart rate 40 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.6° C  Oxygen saturation 95% on room air Which of the following would be the appropriate management?

A 65-year-old patient presents with 2 hours of chest pain that feels like indigestion. In the past medical history, hypertension has been diagnosed, but no evidence of myocardial infarction or angina. This Emergency Department does not have facilities for a percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (see report). Blood pressure 170/94 mmH Heart rate 104 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.6° C Oxygen saturation 95% on room air ECG: ST segment elevation in the anterolateral leads. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial intervention?

A 60-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with heavy retrosternal chest discomfort. The discomfort started 3 days earlier as intermittent brief episodes which became more frequent and prolonged over the last 24 hours. In the Emergency Department he experienced a similar type of discomfort (5/10 on the pain scale of 1-10) which responded well to sublingual nitroglycerin. serial cardiac enzymes are normal (see report). ECG: An initial ECG showed ST segment depression of 0.2 mV in the antero-lateral chest leads, which later normalized completely. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman is brought to the Emergency Department of a tertiary care hospital with rapid onset shortness of breath and left shoulder and arm ache (see image). Blood pressure 100/50 mmHg Heart rate 90 /min Respiratory rate 25 /min Temperature 36.9 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment after the initial Emergency Department management?

A 75-year-old man who has been followed up routinely for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus was found to have an irregular pulse which was not found 6 months earlier. In addition to hypertension and diabetes, his past history confirms a previous transient ischemic attack. He is currently asymptomatic and is compliant with his medications (see report). ECG: Atrial fibrillation at rate of 70 beats per minute. Which of the following is the most appropriate management plan?
choices: Add digoxin to his current treatment regimen
Start anticoagulation therapy to prevent stroke
No further step is needed as he is asymptomatic

question: A 29-year-old woman presents to the Emergency Department complaining of being unable to sleep flat for the last 2 nights due to difficulty in breathing. She has just delivered 1 week earlier. Physical examination confirms a laterally displaced apex beat and the presence of a third heart sound. The jugular veins were distended and bilateral lung crackles could be easily heard. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old man had a myocardial infarction 6 days before. He suddenly develops dyspnoea, cough and frothy sputum. For the first time a harsh systolic murmur is heard over the precordium. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this development?

A 40-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department after fainting while exercising. He reports past episodes of chest pain, which have occurred both at rest and with exercise. On examination of the chest there is I/V systolic ejection murmur heard at the left sternal border, which does not radiate. The intensity of the murmur increases when the patient bears down or stands up. The lung fields are clear (see report). Blood pressure 125/75 mm Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.6° C ECG: Non-specific ST and T wave changes with left atrial enlargement. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 55-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with continuous retrosternal chest pain. An ECG was obtained (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
choices: Acute coronary syndrome with unstable angina

question: 35-year-old women comes to the clinic complaining of infertility for 3 years. She notices excessive breast milk production for 4 months. The physical examination is unremarkable (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 130/80 mmHg Heart rate 80 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.2° C Test Result Normal Values Thyroxine (T4 free) 12.4 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 1.2 0.4 - 5.0 mU/L Prolactin 1452 < 870 pmol/L Brain MRI: Well defined pituitary mass about 0.7 cm, which represent an adenoma. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 55-year-old woman presents with sudden left eye visual loss for 20 minutes. The vision returned to normal after this episode. History reveals, she has diabetes mellitus. The physical examination is normal. Blood pressure 125/75 mmHg Heart rate 75 /min Respiratory rate 16/min Temperature 37.2° C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old woman with congestive heart failure complains of shortness of breath for 3 months. It is precipitated by daily activity at home. The shortness of breath awakened her several times at night. Her medication included fosinopril, carvedilol and furosemide. On  examination, there is bilateral basilar crepitation (see report). Echocardiogram: There is dilated left ventricular chamber. The left ventricular ejection faction is 30%. Blood pressure 125/80 mmH Heart rate 60 /min Respiratory rate 16 /min Temperature 37.1° C Which of the following drugs is indicated?

A 40-year-old man presents to the clinic complaining of numbness of the feet for 1 month. He was diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis 4 months ago. He has been taking isoniazid and rifampin and has 2 months of treatment remaining. He has well controlled diabetes mellitus for the last 3 years. The physical examination is normal. Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 80 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.7° C Which of the following drugs should be given?

A 30-year-old woman with controlled hypothyroidism comes for follow up. She had been sir thyroxin 175 mcg but the dose was increased 3 months ago to 200 mcg. Physical examinatic is normal (see lab results). Blood pressure 130/80 mmH Heart rate 80 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.2° C Test Result Normal Values Thyroxine (T4 free) 12.4 8.5-15.2 pmol/L Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 17.2 0.4-5.0 U/L What is the most likely explanation for these lab findings?

A 45-year-old man was being investigated for hypertension. He was prescribed a drug for his lipid disorder but returned 1 week later with intense face flushing after taking the tablet prescribed. He was then advised to take a full dose of aspirin 3 times daily instead of a low dose once daily. This gave complete relief (see lab results). Tests at first visit  Test Result Normal Values Cholesterol (HDL) 0.72 <1.03 mol/L Cholesterol (LDL) 5.30 <3.36 mol/L Total Cholesterol 6.12 <5.1 mol/L Triglycerides 2.20 <2. 16 mmol/L Alanine aminotransferase 35 5-40 IU/L Creatinine kinase 205 24-195 IU/L Which of the following drugs was he prescribed?

A 45-year-old patient presents to the clinic with a 3-month history of stumbling, weak grip, dysphagia, and generalised weakness, and also had 2 episodes of aspiration pneumonia in the last 2 months. Examination confirms brisk reflexes, spastic muscles, and fasciculation of tongue and thigh. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A man on treatment for multiple sclerosis, presents with acute onset diplopia, ataxia and weakness of the right hand (see report). MRI brain scan: New active lesions compared to previous scans. Which of the following is the best treatment for this development?

A 71-year-old man comes to the Outpatient Clinic with difficulty walking and a hand tremor at rest for the last 3 months. There is no history of trauma or past illness. General examination reveals an expressionless face, slow and slurred speech, and a hand tremor at rest. There is no sensory abnormality but the motor system showed brisk reflexes and hypertonia. The gait is quick, with short steps and diminished associated movements, such as no arm swinging Which of the following is the most probable location of the defect?

A 70-year-old patient presents with a 6-month history of decline in cognitive capacity and conscious level. On examination, the patient has bradykinesia, resting tremors, a mask-like face, and a shuffling gait. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient is having repetitive generalized seizures that continue for 35 minutes. The patient received 20 mg of diazepam intravenously, but there has been no response. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

A 44-year-old woman comes to her physician as she is unable to close her left eye. There is a facial asymmetry, when she smiles and inability to wrinkle the left side of her left forehead. Which of the following nerves is mostly affected?

A 35-year-woman comes to the clinic complaining of severe "pins and needles" sensations on the dorsum of her left hand over parts of the thumb, index and middle fingers. History reveals, she works as a typist. On physical examination, the patient has weakness of wrist dorsiflexion and fingers extension. Which of the following nerves is most likely to be injured?

A 42-year-old woman presents with tiredness and lethargy. She has tingling in her hands and feet. Investigations confirm a megaloblastic anemia. She had a total gastrectomy 3 years ago. Which of the following vitamin deficiencies is most likely to cause these symptoms?

A 45-year-old man presents to the clinic with bilateral ptosis and weakness of the proximal upper and lower limb muscles. Physical examination Is normal except for a positive Simpson test. Edrophonium test Is performed that shows transient improvement in the ptosis (see report). Chest X-ray Normal. Which of the following would be the most suitable treatment?

A 20-year-old woman comes to the Medical Outpatient Department with a large swelling in the front of her neck that she had had for the last 3 years. She also complains of excessive sweating, occasional palpitations, and for the last month, the inability to stay in the kitchen for a long period. She has lost weight despite having a good appetite and intake. The examination of the swelling in her neck showed a soft, nodular mass measuring 8 x 15 cm with an audible bruit. Regional lymph nodes are not palpable (see lab results). Blood pressure 130/85 mmH Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min Temperature 37.0° C Test Result Normal Values Thyroxine (T4 free) 20.2 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 0.1 0.4 - 5.0 U/L Hb 140 120-160 g/L Which of the following is the most appropriate management for palpitations?

A 75-year-old type 2 diabetic undergoes a bowel resection for colon cancer. He is well prior to the operation with well-controlled diabetes and no other underlying condition. The operation is successful and the patient is given postoperative insulin and IV dextrose. 2 days after the operation he becomes very agitated (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Sodium 124 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 3.2 3.5-5.1 mmol/L creatinine 80 44-115 umol/L Blood urea nitrogen 4.6 2.8-8.9 mmol/L Serum osmolality 270 280-300 mmol/kg 24 Urine Analysis Test Result Normal Value Osmolality 310 280-910 mOsm/Kg H20 Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 60-year-old diabetic patient presents for follow-up. Currently, the patient takes metformin that maintains fasting blood glucose levels lower than 5.5 mol/L with HbA1c level of 5.8%. Physical examination is normal, including a lower extremity neurologic examination. The patient has regular eye exams that show no signs of retinopathy. Blood pressure 149/90 mmH (three readings) Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.6° C  Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 25-year-old patient is diagnosed with diabetic ketoacidosis (see lab results). Blood pressure 80/50 mmH Heart rate 140 /min Respiratory rate 26 /min Temperature 36.6° C Test Result Normal Values Random Glucose 52.7 3.9 - 5.5 mol/L Potassium 6 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Bicarbonate 5 21-28 mmol/L Which of the following is the best initial management?
choices: Dopamine drip to raise blood pressure above 90 mm/Hg
2L of normal saline with Kcl 20 mEq/L intravenously
20-unit regular insulin intravenously, followed by 5% dextrose in water at 200 mL/h
Normal saline 2 L as an intravenous bolus and insulin intravenous infusion at 0.1 U/kg/hr

question: A 55-year-old man with a family history of type 2 diabetes undergoes screening (see lab results). Blood pressure 130/85 mmH Heart rate 80 /min Height 185 cm Weight 91 kg Test Result Normal Values Glucose, fasting 7.4 3.5-6.5 mmol/L Hemoglobin A1C 6.3 4.7-5.6% Which of the following should be recommended?

A 55-year-old man with a family history of type 2 diabetes undergoes screening .He gives the history of polyuria (see lab results). A 45-year-old man is diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 3 months ago, and started on metformin 500 mg TDS, comes for his first follow-up (see lab results). A 55-year-old woman has had type 2 diabetes for the past 20 years. She is on an 1800 kcal/day diet and takes metformin 850 mg 3 times a day (see lab results). Blood pressure 130/85 mmHg Heart rate 80 /min Test Result Normal Values Glucose, fasting 7.1 3.5-6.5 mmol/L HA1C 7.8 4.7-5.6 % What should be the target Haemoglobin A1C percentage?
Which of the following findings in the urine would indicate diabetic nephropathy in type 2 diabetes?

A 28-year-old woman developed gestational diabetes during her second pregnancy. She gave birth to a healthy baby 6 months ago. There is a strong family history of type 2 diabetes and now wants to be evaluated for diabetes (see lab resuits). Height 166 cm Weight 91 kg Test Result Normal Values Glucose, fasting 6.5 3.5-6.5 mmol/L bA1C 5.5 4.7-5.6 % Which of the following is the most appropriate therapy?

A 38-year-old man is unable to lose weight despite being on an intensive lifestyle management plan of a low calorie diet and exercise (see lab results). Blood pressure 145/95 mmH Heart rate 80 /min Height 173 cm Weight 125 kg Test Result Normal Values Glucose, fasting 7.1 3.5-6.5 mol/L HbA1C 8.1 4.7-5.6 % Which of the following is the most appropriate advice to reduce weight?

A 66-year-old woman has recently been found to have high blood pressure. She had a cholecystectomy 15 years ago and has osteoarthritis in the knees for which she uses ibuprofen (see lab results). Blood pressure 160/95 mmH Heart rate 84 /min Test Result Normal Values Creatinine 138 44-115 mol/L Sodium 142 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 2.9 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Chloride 100 97-108 mmol/L Bicarbonate 31 21-28 mmol/L Which of the following is the most likely Diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents with a history of 10-day of palpitations, sweating and neck discomfort (see lab results). A 72-year-old patient is evaluated for mid-thoracic back pain. The patient does not smoke cigarettes and rarely drinks alcohol. The only medications taken are aspirin, calcium supplements, and a multivitamin. Very few dairy products are consumed. On physical examination, the patient has a mild dorsal kyphosis with mild tenderness over the mid and lower thoracic regions (see lab results and report). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents with a 3-day history of seizures (see lab results). A 36-year-old patient presents with a 6-month history of decreased libido and weak erections (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Prolactin 2100 < 870 pmol/L Follicle-stimulating hormone 12 5-20 IU/L  Luteinizing hormone 18 5-22 U/L Which of the following is the next most useful investigation?

A 30-year-old man presents with a history of increased urine output, especially during the night and increased thirst for the past 2 months (see report). Water deprivation test: Serum osmolality above normal without adequate concentration of urine osmolality; no response to desmopressin administration. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient complains of irritability, heat intolerance and recent onset of heart palpitations. The neck examination is normal. (see lab results). A patient with hypothyroidism, on 0.025 mg of L-thyroxin, complains of fatigue, cold intolerance, and weight gain (see lab result). choices: Increase L-thyroxin and check TSH in 6 weeks
Increase L-thyroxin and check TSH in 3 weeks
Decrease L-thyroxin and check TSH in 6 weeks
Decrease L-thyroxin and check TSH in 3 weeks

question: A 35-year-old man complains of discomfort in both breasts with milk production when expressed manually for a month. It has been associated with headache and low sexual interest. He has been married for 3 years and his wife has not been able to become pregnant. On examination, he has mild acne on his face (see lab results). Weight 97 kg Height 173 cm Test Result Normal Values Thyroxine (T4 free) 8.4 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 6.8 0.4 - 5.0 U/L Follicle-stimulating hormone 5.8 5-20 IU/L Luteinizing hormone 7.1 5-22 U/L Prolactin 2350 < 870 pmol/L which of the following is the most likely visual field defect?

A 32-year-old woman complains that her menstrual cycle has stopped for the last 9 months. She also has discomfort in both breasts with milk production when expressed manually. Her sexual drive has been decreased for the last year. She has been married for 3 years and failed to become pregnant. The physical examination is normal and pregnancy test is negative (see lab results). A 44-year-old woman presents with a neck swelling for the last 2 months. It is associated with frequent bowel movement, increased appetite and weight loss. A 28-year-old woman presents with a painful neck swelling for the last week. The swelling has been increasing over time. She has a sore throat and difficulty in swallowing. She has frequent bowel motions. On a physical examination, there is a diffuse tender anterior neck swelling and both hands show a fine tremor (see lab results). A 45-year-old woman comes to the clinic for a follow-up. She was started on levothyroxine for treatment of hypothyroidism 2 weeks before (see lab result). Test Result Normal Value TSH 7.5 0.4-6.5 mU/L Which of the following would be the best treatment plan?
choices: Same dose, check TSH level in 1 to 2 months
Reduce dose, check TSH level in 1 to 2 months
Reduce dose, check TSH level in 48 to 72 hours

question: A 23-year-old pregnant patient complains of irritability and sweating. On examination, she is thin and appears anxious. Her thyroid gland is nodular, diffusely enlarged, but not tender. A patient has presented with a 2 cm solid thyroid nodule on the Ultrasound. Which of the following is the best next step in the management?

A 26-year-old woman has become increasingly tired for the past 2 months. During the past week she has noted purple blotches on her skin. On physical examination, there are petechial haemorrhages on her trunk and extremities (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Hb 72 120-160 g/L HCT 0.22 0.37-0.48 MCV 92 80-95 fl WBC 1.5 4.5-10.5 x 109/L  Platelet count 10 150-400 x 109/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old man presents to the clinic with headaches and increased tiredness for the last 4 months. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man comes to the Outpatient Clinic because of the recent development of marked peripheral edema. He has no significant past medical history. Urinalysis: Oval fat bodies, and some hyaline casts and occasional RBCs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old overweight man presents to the general physician with 6-month of intermittent epigastric burning pain. He has also noted that for the past 2 months he has been experiencing episodes of nausea, an unpleasant taste in the mouth, hoarseness, and a nocturnal cough. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old man with Gastro Esophageal Reflux Disease presents to the general physician with 3-month history of intermittent retrosternal burning pain, worse on bending, nausea, regurgitation with an unpleasant taste in the mouth, and a nocturnal cough. The patient has been using over the counter antacids with no relief. Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?
An individual who has received all 3 doses of hepatitis B vaccine and has never had hepatitis B virus infection. Which of the following serologic markers is expected to be positive?

A 53-year-old woman presents to the Outpatient Department. She has been unwell for 6 months with arthralgia, fever, weight loss and more recently has developed pleuritic chest pains. She also has synovitis of the small joints of the hands. There were no rashes or nail fold infarcts. Heart sounds are normal (see lab results and reports). What is the immunological status of a patient with negative HBsAg, positive anti-HBc and positive anti-HBs?
choices: Immune due to hepatitis B vaccination

question: A 45-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of episodes of pain with swelling and warmth of her hands and feet for the past 3 weeks. Over the next 6 years, her hands become deformed so that it is difficult to perform tasks as simple as opening a door or buttoning her blouse. A 43-year-old patient man presents with headache and neck stiffness (see reports). CSF Analysis: Appearance cloudy Glucose low Protein high White cells 100 /mm3 (70% polymorphs) CT Brain: Normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the infection?

A 22-year-old man presents with altered sensorium for the last 2 days and headaches for 5 days, with a history of fever for the preceding month. choices: Send sputum for Acid fast bacilli

question: A 47-year-old patient presents with 12-hour of severe pain and swelling of the right first metatarsophalangeal joint. On examination, the affected joint is erythematous and tender. Blood pressure 110/ 65 mmHg Heart rate 105 /min Respiratory rate 12 /min Temperature 38°C Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 52-year-old patient presents with isolated pain and swelling of the left knee. Arthrocentesis demonstrates innumerable needle-shaped negatively birefringent crystals. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 32-year-old woman complains of severe joint pain in the fingers of both hands, especially in the morning during the winter months. Examination confirms deformity of her fingers (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 74-year-old woman complains of a deep, aching pain of the hip which is aggravated by walking. She states that after a busy day, the pain keeps her awake at night, and each morning her hip is stiff for several hours. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the pain?

A 60-year-old woman complains of pain in her right knee for the last 3 years. The pain is worse with activity and relieved by rest and analgesics. Physical examination reveals that she has a varus knee deformity and tenderness over the medial joint line (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old man presents to the Outpatient Clinic with very severe pain, swelling and redness of the first metatarsophalangeal joint. Some joint fluid is withdrawn (see lab results and reports). Test Result Normal Values Colour yellow clear Clarity opaque transparent WBC per mm3 100,000 < 200 PMNs 75 < 25% Fluid Exam: Negatively birefringent rate crystals are seen on polarizing examination of the synovial fluid. Hands X-ray: Juxta-articular punched-out sclerotic erosions involving the first metatarsophalangeal and interphalangeal joints with associated periarticular soft tissue swelling. Which of the following treatments should be avoided in the current situation?
Which of the following crystals is responsible for the arthritic symptoms of pseudogout?
A 29-year-old woman is diagnosed with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. Which of the following pathological changes is characteristic of this diagnosis?

A young man comes into the clinic with intermittent haemoptysis for 2 months, associated with some blood in his urine. He is a non-smoker and was previously in excellent health. He also describes a weight gain of 20 kg over the past 3 weeks, with "puffy eyes" in the morning. He has an elevated serum creatinine concentration (see report). Lung Biopsy: Serum immunoglobulin on basement membranes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following sites is the best to aspirate a sample of right pleural effusion with a syringe and needle?

A 45-year-old man presents with difficulty in breathing and a nocturnal cough for the last 3 weeks. Spirometry results show a forced vital capacity and the FEV/FVC ratio lower than normal. Which of the following consistent with these findings?
What is the optimal treatment for community-acquired pneumonia in an otherwise healthy patient?
What is the optimal duration of anticoagulation following an initial episode of pulmonary embolism?
In which of the following conditions is interstitial pneumonitis a characteristic histopathologic finding?
Which of the following pneumoconiosis will commonly predispose to the development of pulmonary tuberculosis?
A 38-year-old woman with pleurisy requires a thoracentesis. The needle should be placed on the midaxillary line of the affected side. Which rib level should the needle penetrate through?

A 72-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with fever, night sweats and cough for 2 weeks (see report). Chest X-ray: Right upper lobe consolidation.  Which of the following is the best next step in management?
choices: Admit the patient to the Intensive Unit
Isolate the patient in a single, negative pressure room

question: Which of the following can improve survival in patients with severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease?

A 25-year-old patient with moderate persistent asthma is currently on a low-dose, inhaled corticosteroid but needs to use a beta-2 agonist rescue inhaler at least once a day. Which of the following should be added to the current treatment?
choices: Leukotriene inhibitor to the steroid regimen
Long-acting beta-2 agonist to steroid regimen

question: A 55-year-old patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presents with shortness of breath. The patient is in severe respiratory distress and hypoxemic with decreased breath sounds and a prolonged expiration phase. There is no improvement after bronchodilators. The patient is conscious with a pH of 7.3. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
Which of the following is the most effective treatment for adults with obstructive sleep apnea?
choices: Maintain a BMI less than 30 kg/m2

question: A 28-year-old patient with mild intermittent asthma, has daytime symptoms about once to twice a week, and none at night. Which of the following initial treatment should be given when necessary?

A 28-year-old woman has had mild intermittent asthma for years. She uses a short-acting  bronchodilator, as needed. Over the past 2 months, she has noticed that she is using her inhaler at least 3 times a week, and on occasions has had to wake up in the middle of the night to use her inhaler. Which of the following treatments should be added?

A 55-year-old man presents with shortness of breath and a productive cough. The patient has a history of smoking. On auscultation, there is wheezing throughout the chest (see reports). Chest X-ray: Normal. Arterial Blood Gases: Normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient suddenly develops chest pain and dyspnoea. Vocal and tactile fremitus are reduced, and breath sounds are diminished (see report). Chest X-ray: It shows absent lung markings on the left side. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most likely cause of lobar pneumonia in adults?

A 45-year-old man is admitted with general tiredness and fever. There is a past history of a chest infection of 4-week duration, for which he was given oral antibiotics. He felt better initially. but never fully recovered and is now becoming worse (see report). Chest X-ray: It shows a right-sided pleural effusion. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old nurse working in the pulmonary clinic, complains of fever and a productive cough for the last 3 months. She has received 2 courses of oral antibiotics, but showed no  improvement (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the clinic with shortness of breath and a cough productive of yellow sputum for the past 2 days. There has also been blood-stained sputum for the last 3 hours. The patient has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes a day for the past 35 years. On examination, there are rhonchi, wheezing, and crepitations heard over the right hemothorax (see report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 84 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 38.8° C Oxygen saturation 95% on room air Chest X-ray: It shows a dense infiltrate in the right lower lobe. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman with asthma has not had a severe attack for the last 3 months. However she has a history of cough and wheezing 2-3 times each week. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 21-year-old woman comes to the clinic with episodes of shortness of breath on exertion for one year. She has to stop after 15-20 minutes of exercise, because of dyspnoea and coughing, which get better after about one hour of rest. There are no symptoms at rest. Physical examination and spirometry are normal. Blood pressure 125/75 mmH Heart rate 80 /min Respiratory rate 12 /min Temperature 37.0° C Which of the following is the most appropriate inhaled treatment before exercise?

A 42-year-old man with asthma presents with daily symptoms despite regularly using a long acting -agonist inhaler and an inhaled high-dose corticosteroid. He also uses a short acting -  agonist inhaler as "rescue" medication. These episodes also wake him from sleep 2-3 times a week. Physical examination shows bilateral (see table). Blood pressure 140/85 mmH Heart rate 90 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.7° C Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second Normal value Before bronchodilator 65 % 25-75 % After bronchodilators 91 % Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
choices: Observe the patient using his inhaler

question: A 67-year-old patient presents to the Emergency Department with chest pain, shortness of breath, and haemoptysis following a car trip for more than 5 hours (see report). ECG: Right axis deviation, an S1-Q3-T3 pattern, and a right bundle branch block. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old smoker presents to a clinic with progressive shortness of breath (see report). Chest X-ray: It reveals a massive right pleural effusion. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
A 28-year-old patient develops the sudden onset of dyspnoea and tachycardia 5 days post a knee surgery. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient with stage IIIB small cell lung cancer complains of new onset of back pain for the past 12 hours. Initial neurological examination is normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate action to take?
choices: High dose IV corticosteroids and MRI

question: On a follow-up consultation of a patient with a squamous cell carcinoma, some abnormalities are noted in blood analysis (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Parathyroid hormone 1.0 1.1-5.3 pmol/L Calcium 3.30 2.15-2.62 mmol/L Calcium ionised 1.6 1.1-1.3 mmol/L Sodium 140 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 4.3 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Which of the following is the most likely cause of the metabolic abnormality?
choices: Secretion of PTH-related peptide by the tumour

question: A 78-year-old man and current smoker, with 50 pack-year smoking history, complains of shortness of breath, dry cough and fatigue progressing over the past 8 weeks. The patient also reports a significant weight loss, corresponding to approximately 15% of body weight over the last 12 weeks. Physical examination is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old man with sickle cell anemia presents with right sided chest pain and shortness of breath for 2 days. It was associated with pain in both legs and back. On examination, fine crackles were heard in right middle and lower zones (see image). Blood pressure 125/75 mmHg Heart rate 92 /min Respiratory rate 25/min Temperature 37.9° C Oxygen saturation 91% on room air Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old man with sickle cell anemia presents with right sided chest pain and shortness of breath for 2 days. It is associated with pain in both legs and back. On examination, fine crackles are heard in right middle and lower zones (see image). Blood pressure 125/75 mmHg Heart rate 92 /min Respiratory rate 25 /min Temperature 37.9° C Oxygen saturation 91% on room air What is the most effective drug to reduce this incidence?

A 78-year-old man presents with 2-year history of slow and progressive deterioration in his memory. The patient is able to perform some activities of daily living, including dressing and bathing. His personality has changed from that of a kind and caring person into someone who has periods of agitation and aggression. Neurologic and musculoskeletal examination cannot be carried out. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the peak of nicotine withdrawal symptoms after smoking cessation?
Which of the following is an alternative treatment for severe depression?
Which of the following is the antidote for an opiate overdose?
Which of the following is the most likely side effect of bupropion when prescribed for smoking cessation?

A 24-year-old inactive woman presents to the clinic with 5-month history of amenorrhea. On examination, she has a body mass index of 20, stable for the last 5 years (see lab results). Pregnancy test:  Negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following factors is the most important in determining the success of a smoking cessation program?

A 45-year-old man newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes presents to the clinic for futhur management. He is on time for the appointment, but because of an emergency case, the physician arrive late to the clinic. When the physician walks in, the patient appears extremely angry. Which of the following is the most appropriate response by the physician?
choices: Explore the reasons for the anger
Help the patient understand their anger
Empathise with newly diagnosed diabetic patient

question: A 56-year-old man presents to the clinic for evaluation. The physician has difficulty in obtaining accurate information regarding reason of attendance. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in consultation?
choices: Use medical terms that the patient understands
Control the interview with direct questions
Involve the patient in the treatment plan

question: A 76-year-old man admitted with diagnosis of pneumonia has fluctuating levels of attention, changes in awareness, and a marked disturbance of the sleep/wake cycle. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
choices: Isolation in a quiet, dark room
Allow a relative to stay with the patient

question: A 27-year-old woman delivered a healthy baby 3 months ago. She is currently undergoing psychotherapy for postpartum depression. Which of the following is the most appropriate to be added to optimize treatment?
choices: Prescribe very small doses of imipramine

question: A 23-year-old man complains of having an unusually prominent jaw. He has been seen by 3 plastic surgeons, but each one has refused to do anything. On examination, he appears depressed and has no visible protrusion, the jaw and face are normal. He has past medical  history of rhinoplasty and blepharoplasty. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 41-year-old man presents to the clinic requesting a complete examination to exclude colon cancer. He recently had some investigations done and provided a list of test results. He complains that this fear is interfering severely with his work and social activities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is a prediction of the feeling of hopelessness?

A 20-year-old woman presents to the clinic with history of abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, localized weakness to the right leg, and has a history of irregular menses. In the past, she has sought treatment for head, back, joint, and chest pain. Factitious disorder and malingering have been excluded as diagnoses. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following investigations should be recommended for elderly patient with cognitive deficit?

An 8-year-old boy recently moved to another city. Soon after moving, school started, but the boy  hesitated to make friends with anyone and had a hard time paying attention in class. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old man presents for a routine visit, while reporting his medical history, he reveals a significant alcohol intake. The physician wants to assess the drinking further using the cut- annoyed-guilty-eye (CAGE) screening questionnaire. Which of the following is a question in the CAGE screening questionnaire?
choices: "Do you eat more after you drink?"
"Do you think you are an alcoholic?"
"Have you ever felt guilty about your drinking?"

question: A 46-year-old woman presents to the clinic with 8-month history of irritability, excessive worry, and difficulty falling asleep and concentrating. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old woman is concerned about losing her job because of tiredness and would like to take antidepressants because of having a difficult time falling asleep and geeng up in the morning. Her sleep disturbance is related to the inability to relax after geeng into bed. She is repeatedly checks to make sure that the door is locked, the oven is off, and the children's school supplies are organized. A similar routine occurs in the morning. She states that her behaviour is out of control but if is not done, she will not be able to sleep or leave the house. Which of the following disorders is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old healthy man presents to the clinic with a 3-month history of feeling depressed. He is distressed at work and burnt-out. 4 months earlier, he was promoted to a managerial position and was having an interpersonal conflict with 2 of the employees. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

An 18-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with 20-minute history of light- headedness, headaches, and nausea. He complains of tingling around the mouth and in the  fingertips. On examination, he is anxious, tremulous, sweating, and breathing heavily. Which of the following is the most appropriate first action?
choices: Patient rebreathe into a paper bag

question: Which of the following atypical antipsychotic agents is associated with the most weight gain?
Which of the following is the best treatment for a generalized anxiety disorder?
For which of the following childhood psychiatric disorders, clozapine is the most appropriate medication?
Which of the following antidepressants has a high efficacy in childhood and adolescent depression?
A 30-year-old man presents to the clinic with 3-month history of aliens taking to him and pueng thoughts into his mind? Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 55-year-old man presents to the clinic with history of difficulty maintaining erections and impotence that occurs during stressful periods of life. He is currently under stress at work. On examination, he has normal physical findings. Which of the following is the first step in management?
choices: Refer to a urologist for evaluation

question: A 38-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of recurrent intense fear accompanied by irritability, excessive worry, palpitations, and chest tightness. She is avoiding social gathering fearing of having same symptoms. Physical examination findings are normal. Which of the following medications is the most appropriate first line of treatment?

A 5-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his mother with history of impaired language development, impaired intelligence, compulsive repetitive behavior, and a preoccupation with inanimate objects. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A mother of a 3 month-old baby presents to the clinic and tells the physician that she is "going crazy." She states that since the baby has been born, she has continuously visualized a snake crawling into the baby's crib at night. She states that she knows it is not likely to happen but cannot get the thought out of her mind. She checks the baby's crib up to 50 times per night to ensure that there is no snake. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old woman presents to the clinic with history of anxiety. 2 months ago, during a meeting at her job, she became very anxious, sweaty, and short of breath. She had to leave the meeting in order to calm down. Since then, she has avoided meeting rooms out of fear that she will have a recurrence of her symptoms. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man presents to the clinic with history of gradual fear of automobiles. He has always been anxious of cars, but now can no longer look at them without experiencing shortness of breath, sweating, and fear. Which of the following disorders is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old woman presents to the clinic with history of red dry skin on her hands. She washes her hands up to 70 times per day because she always feels dirty. Washing her hands relieves her anxiety, but as she touches anything, she wants to wash again. Which of the following disorders is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man with a history of drug abuse presents to the clinic weekly with a variety of health complaints, which vary each time, and are greatly exaggerated. When he is unaware of being observed he appears asymptomatic. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old woman presents to the clinic for a routine physical check-up. On examination, she has fine hair all over the body. She feels fat and subsequently diets. BMI 16.8 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman calls the clinic expressing fear of leaving the house, and has been inside for 2 months. She becomes anxious at the thought of walking out the front door and is now unable to enter the room containing the front door. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man presents to the clinic with history of sweating, palpitations, nausea, and a "panicky feeling" when required to deliver a speech at work. He has no other difficulties at work. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old woman presents to the clinic with history of constant counting of floor tiles, cars, items on a dinner plate, and words in a conversation. She is upset by the counting but becomes anxious and agitated when she tries to stop herself from counting. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 61-year-old man presents with history of constantly thinks about aliens landing in his backyard, especially when away from home. Despite knowing that aliens do not exist, he feels overwhelmed with the idea that they have landed. He fears that he is "going insane" Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old man presents to the clinic with history of hearing voices coming from the toaster and refrigerator, warning that all the food is poisoned. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man presents to the clinic for routine check-up. On examination, he kept looking to the right frequently. When questioned, he said, "My mother is there, but no one can see her except me". He claims that she comes and goes, even though the family indicates she died when the patient was a child. which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 17-year-old man with history of intravenous drug abuse presents to the clinic for clinical evaluation. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in investigation?

A 17-year-old high school athlete presents to the clinic for an annual physical check-up. On examination, he has gained 20 Kg in the past 4 months and has very well developed musculature of the upper body, acne over the face and back and foul breath. Heart rate 94 /min Temperature 37.6° C Blood pressure 138/89 mmHg Respiratory rate 14 /min Which of the following the patient should be screened for?

A 52-year-old man presents to the clinic for a routine physical check-up. He has a history of pulling out hair when under stress. On examination, he has diffuse hair thinning along with the absence of eyelashes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old girl presents to the clinic with history of tetany, swollen glands, and eroded dental enamel (see lab result). Electrolytes test Result Normal Value Potassium 2.8 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old drug addict man presents to the Emergency Department with 1-hour history of unconsciousness. On examination, he has pinpoint pupils and a respiratory rate of 8/minute. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 53-year-old woman with history of depression presents to the Emergency Department with history of nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, tinnitus, and shortness of breath 6 hours after consuming 50 tablets of aspirin (see lab result). Test Result Normal Value Plasma salicylate concentration 54 15-30 mg/dL which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

A 34-year-old healthy man presents to the clinic with a 2-year history of worsening sad mood, poor appetite, insomnia, fatigue, low self-esteem, and feeling of hopelessness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old girl is brought to the clinic by her mother with a bald patch on her scalp. Her mother noted that she plucks her hair while studying and under stress. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 20-year-old man presents to the clinic with poor personal hygiene, echolalia, echopraxia, muttering to self, sieng in an odd posture for hours, and insomnia for the past 2 months. On examination, his orientation and memory are normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 45-year-old woman presents to the Primary Health Care Clinic with symptoms of anxiety due to difficulties in her relationship with her co-workers. Her examination was normal and the doctor has decided that there is no need for any investigation. Which of the following would be the most effective approach for counselling?
choices: Instructing how to deal with others

question: A 55-year-old smoker presents to the Primary Health Care Clinic for the result of the biopsy of a lesion in his right lung. When informed that, he has a cancer in his right lung, he asked with anxiety, "is it a mistake?" Which of the following is the most appropriate description for the patient's reaction?

A 30-year-old man presents to the clinic with 10-month history of restlessness, difficulty concentrating, and disturbance in his sleep pattern. He is diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder.  Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

An 18-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with 1-week history of euphoria, increased blood pressure, tachycardia, nausea, weight loss, psychomotor agitation, chills, sweating and visual hallucinations. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old child is brought to the clinic for his yearly physical examination. His history revealed various behavioral issues, including poor interaction with peers and family, delayed language development, repetitive movements and difficulty of accepting change. The child stiffens physically when touched, does not respond to the examiner and does not make eye contact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old woman is admitted to the Psychiatric Unit after causing superficially lacerations to her wrists. The reason is that she felt that her therapist has abandoned her. She has depressed mood that varies by the hour. On admission, she claimed that she has heard a voice speaking to her, although she currently denies it. She caused a disagreement between the psychiatric resident and the nursing staff, who have conflicting views of her behaviour in the unit. which of the following personality disorders is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with irritability, suspiciousness, over activity and poor hygiene. Emergency Department doctors regarded his behaviour as abnormal and called for a psychiatrist. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old man presents to the clinic with a history of a disturbed recent memory as a cardinal feature of his disturbed state of mind along with behavioural changes. which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man presents to the clinic complaining of reduced energy, lack of enjoyment, reduced sleep, reduced appetite, suicidal ideas and lack of self-confidence. Examination and lab results are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old was brought to the Emergency Department complaining that his neighbours are trying to harm him and are ploeng to kill him. On questioning, he was very sure about this and said that he is still hearing their voices talking with each other, though none of them were present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old woman presents to the Psychiatric Outpatient Clinic with history of psychomotor excitation and irritability. She has grandiose delusions and auditory hallucinations. On a mental state examination, she exhibited a lack of insight and flight of ideas. Which of the following disorders is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old man presents to the clinic with 2-year history of geeng orgasm too readily during the sexual act. He complains that during the sexual intercourse he is having palpitations and worrying thoughts in his mind all the time. On examination, he has normal findings. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old girl presents for a follow-up visit complaining that she is unable to eat because of an intense desire to reduce her weight. Some time she develops an impulse to eat excessively and she then follows the impulse. She then intermittently self-induces vomiting. On examination, she looked weak. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old student presents to the Psychiatric Outpatient Clinic complaining that she feels embarrassed, dizzy, and tremulous whenever she tries to answer verbally in the classroom. Which of the following is the best treatment?

A 21-year-old man with depression presents for follow-up visit. During the consultation, the psychiatrist asked, "Do you think that you are mentally ill?" Which of the following findings is the psychiatrist wants to assess?

A 23-year-old college student was brought to the Psychiatric Outpatient Clinic with a 3-month history of persecutory delusions, hearing voices commenting on his actions, and disorganized behaviour without disturbance of mood, then returning to normal with no medication. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old man presents to the clinic for routine visit. During the consultation, he speaks loudly and rapidly without completely expressing one thought before beginning another. Speech patterns are rhyming and the patient is easily distracted by cues in the immediate surroundings. Which of the following is the most likely description for these findings?

A 22-year-old man presents to the clinic with history of approaching strangers and asking them the same inappropriate question without stopping when instructed to do so. The patient seemed unaware of the fact that this was an inappropriate behaviour. Which of the following is the most likely description for this behaviour?

A mother brings her 2-week-old infant to the Well-Baby Clinic for a check-up. During the visit, the physician found the child to be normal but the mother gives inappropriate answers to the questions. She appeared disoriented in time and date. She states that the child is deformed and unlikely to live long.  Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman presents to the clinic for postpartum care. She has experienced tearfulness and irritability during the 1 week following the delivery of her child. This episode resolved spontaneously and her mood has been normal since then. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
- a +  Which of the following conditions is most often associated with manic behaviour?

A 21-year-old woman presents to the clinic with history of changes in the voice that she hears. Until now, it had been merely making critical comments about everything she did. For the past 2 weeks, however, she thinks the voices seemed to have been able to "suck thoughts out" of her and send them to others. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old man presents to the clinic with history of unusual behaviour. He keeps a blanket over the television believing that the government uses the actors to spy through the TV. He believes that the instructions to cover the TV came from God who spoke through the light bulb. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old healthy man complains of episodes of chest tightness, palpitations, dizziness and breathlessness. These episodes resolved after about 5 minutes. He remains normal between episodes and the interval may extend for several days before a new episode occurs. He has had constant anxiety about having another attack and feels sad about the situation. The patient cannot identify a triggering mechanism. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man gives a history of pancreatic carcinoma and reports having lost all his prescriptions. He says that despite having recently completed chemotherapy he has developed new symptoms and is afraid of a recurrence. There is no medical records for him in the hospitals. When confronted with this information, the patient ran away from the clinic. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old woman presents to the clinic with 2-month history of a sleep disturbance, loss of interest, low energy, poor memory, and suicidal ideation. On examination, she looks weak and inactive. Laboratory investigations are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old healthy man is brought to the clinic for evaluation of progressive erratic behaviour. Over the past 4 months, he has believed that people on television are reading his thoughts. He expressed the presence of supernatural powers and that he has begun to act out in response to these ideations. He has not caused injuries, but the trends are becoming more violent. On examination, he is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most appropriate management plan for major depression?
choices: Select any drug to start as all have equal efficacy
Initiate therapy with one medication for 2 weeks
Change medications if the patient doesn't respond

question: Which of the following systems is stimulated by stressful situation?

Stress leads to an increase in cortisol and catecholamine secretion that can alter the levels of  lymphocyte production that fight disease. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for these effect?
Which of the following is the main difference between delirium and dementia?

A 72-year-old man experiences inability to sustain attention, disorganized thinking, hallucinations, and disorientation commencing 12 hours after an aortic femoral popliteal bypass. The symptoms fluctuated during the next 2 days. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old man with Alzheimer's dementia becomes agitated and aggressive after developing hallucinations and delusions. A complete evaluation does not reveal any environmental, medical, or psychiatric cause and behavioural interventions failed to improve the agitation. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 78-year-old man is brought to the Outpatient Clinic with a 2-year history of slow and progressive deterioration in his memory. He is able to perform some activities of daily living. including dressing and bathing as well as cooking. He has personality changes, once a kind and caring parent he now displays periods of both agitation and aggression. Neurologic and musculoskeletal examination cannot be carried out. Which of the following is the best management?
choices: Admission to a chronic care facility

question: A 30-year-old man presents to the Outpatient Clinic with manifestations of opioid withdrawal. After full investigations, he was diagnosed as a heroin addict. As part of the rehabilitation process, he was prescribed a substitute for the addictive drug. Which of the following drugs should be prescribed?
Which of the following is described as "False belief not in accordance with a person's intelligence or culture"?

A 65-year-old man with congestive heart failure and osteoarthritis moved into a nursing home 3 months ago. During the past 4 weeks, the patient has lost 3.6 kg, lost interest in all social activities, and has been crying almost every day. The mood is worse in the morning. At times, especially when the mood is impaired, the patient's short-term memory appears to be lost. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old girl presents with a 12 kg weight loss over the last 6 months. She feels fat with an intense fear of gaining weight. Over the last 4 months, the patient has had amenorrhea. On examination, she has lanugo hair distribution. Height 167 cm weight 42 kg Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman presents to the clinic with recurrent attacks of palpitations, chest pain, difficulty in breathing, and a fear of dying. She also trembles, experiences numbness and tingling sensations in the hands and feet. The past medical history is not significant. On examination, she looks tense, and the hands are cold with fine tremors. Heart rate 108 /min, regular Temperature 37.2° C Blood pressure 120/82 mmHg Respiratory rate 14 /min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old man presents with a 2-year history of intense fear before giving classes as a teacher in a secondary school. He claims that it is only a matter of time before a major teaching mistake is made.  Which of the following phobias is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old man presents to the clinic with 2 months history of anxiety, irritability, impotence, difficulty in sleeping, and a weight loss of 10 kg.
